I will do it much like last year, just tighten it a little because fertilizer and labor both cost money. I am old now, and with only 2 people in the house and 5 mu total, I will not make things too complicated. On my wheat-maize land, I will keep 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is steady and I know what it can give me with well water. The other 2 mu I will keep in cotton, because cotton still brings cash if I keep the weeds, worms, and aphids under control. I only finished primary school, so I do not talk big theory, but after farming this many years I do look at the land and the crop color. If wheat seedlings are weak, I will not be stingy with topdressing. If maize wants to grow ears, I will feed it enough nitrogen. For cotton, I will not save too much on fertilizer or sprays, because once cotton falls behind, it is hard to catch up. Around here I also watch what other farmers do. If the neighbors use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize and get better grain, I will follow that. I will plough before wheat and cotton, and for maize after wheat harvest I will usually use rotary tillage to save time and catch the moisture. With well irrigation, I will water wheat more, maize a couple of times if rain is short, and cotton a few times at key stages. I would rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose yield, because a poor harvest hurts much more than wasting one small bag.
